function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** (in this context) refers to an official authorization or instruction given to someone—typically a financial institution—to act on behalf of another party. In banking and finance, it’s most commonly used when:

1. **Direct Debit Mandate** – A customer authorizes a bank or payment service provider to collect recurring payments from their account automatically (e.g., utility bills, subscription fees).  
2. **Investment Mandate** – An investor gives a fund manager permission to invest money according to agreed terms.

Key points:
| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Parties involved** | Principal (the person giving authority), Agent/Institution (who performs actions) |
| **Scope** | Can cover one transaction, periodic collections, or broader investment powers |
| **Legal basis** | Usually governed by local regulations; often requires written confirmation |
| **Revocation** | Principals can cancel at any time, subject to notice periods |

In your system, “mandates” likely refer to records stored for each authorized action (like direct debits). Partners may request lists of such mandates via APIs (`partner_mandates` or `user_mandates`) filtered by status (“active”, “pending”, “inactive”).
